summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for acute kidney injury with a creatinine rise from 1.7 to 2.8. The etiology was attributed to elevated tacrolimus levels, likely contributing to his recent headache and fatigue. Tacrolimus was held initially, and losartan and spironolactone were discontinued due to hyperkalemia and concerns for pre-renal injury. Renal ultrasound showed a normal transplant kidney, ruling out rejection. The patient completed a two-week course of IV antibiotics for ongoing osteomyelitis treatment, switching from ertapenem to meropenem. His kidney function improved, creatinine returned to baseline, and he was discharged home on his prior medications with follow-up plans.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
